When and why did you start training for fighting? I started doing Ashihara Karate 15 years ago because I got bullied around at school by some wannabe tough guys and wanted to learn how to defend myself. I quickly started competing in Ashihara Karate. Five years after that I discovered MMA and was both frightened and intrigued by it. I wondered if I could get good at it.

Training: I do technical training in the morning and sparring/heavy drilling at night. Besides that, I also find the time during the week to do some cardio training and weightlifting.

What ranks and titles have you held? Fightergalla WW Champion, European MMA (yes, that was really the name of the promotion) WW champion, Cage Warriors WW champion.

Do you have any heroes? Not really. I have some people I look up to but I don't have a hero per se.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means a lot. It's both a stamp of approval and it's the possibility to start a new chapter in my MMA career. I've been dreaming of one day fighting in the UFC since I started doing MMA.

What was your job before you started fighting? Technical IT Customer Supporter

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I won all my amateur fights besides the very first one. My third fight ended with a KO that was named KO of the Year by the Danish martial arts magazine, Fighter.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Has the record for the fastest KO in Scandinavia with a six-second KO.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Karate green belt. BJJ brown belt

Favorite grappling technique: Arm triangle.

Favorite Striking technique: Kicks

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started at 9 years old with Karate. By my father’s influence, he wanted me to practice a physical activity and learn self-defense. Then I started to compete, stand out and love it so much. 

What professional titles have you held? Brazilian Karate Champion, Paranaense Karatê Champion, Karate World Champion, Paranaense Jiu-Jitsu Champion, UAEJJF Jiu-Jitsu National Pro Champion And a few Muay Thai fights 

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Only one Muay Thai fight

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Jiu-Jitsu Purple Belt 

Any belts/ ranks in striking disciplines? Brown Belt Karate, ⁠Dark Blue and Black Muay Thai 

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? I feel like I didn’t have a toughest fight because all my fights were tough. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? I have a lot of fighters that I like… Poatan, Ronda, Namajunas, Marina Rodriguez, Charles do Bronxs, St Pierre. Everyone is an amazing fighter - I admire their history and fight style. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, I studied law but I didn’t finish, I stopped in the last year. I had to choose between fighting professionally or college and my heart chose fighting.

What was your job before you started fighting? I always taught Muay Thai for women, until 2022. I manage the gym that I train at, and I was a partner, so I take care of all the paperwork and functional parts. 

Personal Life / Background: I'm engaged to a fighter, Marcel Adur, a great name on the national scene, I love to dance; if I didn't become a fighter, I would definitely be a dancer. I have many pets and I love them very much, they are my children and I made them all live in harmony - 3 pitbulls with two cats and a cockatiel, and I intend to have a mini goat, maybe a place with many animals. I love reading and I love practicing any sport.

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I tried out an MMA class in 2008 and from the first punch I knew I could do this.

Training: A typical day of training for me is waking up at 6am, training until noon, then rest or hang out with my family until about 5pm. Then I’ll take my kids to the kids’ class at our gym and I’ll do my hard training from about 7 to 10pm. 

What ranks and titles have you held? Fight Time Promotions Welterweight Title & Elite Promotions Amateur Welterweight Title

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Anderson Silva, because of his dominating career

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means I'm blessed, I'm supposed to be here, and that all my hard work wasn't a waste.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? The Randy Brown hammerfist KO. It let me know I can finish the fight from anywhere and anything can happen.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Jesus and my wife because she has been with me since the beginning

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? For a short time, I studied criminal justice and it wasn't for me.

What was your job before you started fighting? Landscaping & I own my own pressure washing business.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Amateur record of 9-0, 2-0 in kickboxing and countless grappling completion placements.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Jiu-Jitsu brown belt

Favorite grappling technique: Guillotine

Favorite Striking technique: Superman punch to spinning backfist

Besides titles and money, what motivates you? My wife and 7 children 

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: My wife and I have been married 15 years, we have 7 kids from 1 to 13 years old, a dog, chickens, ducks and fish. I love fishing, spending time with family and watching our kids do the things they love.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training from the age of five; it’s all I’ve ever known. I kept up the training in honor of my late father, and it has now blossomed into a successful professional career.

What professional titles have you held? The People’s Championship. Still reigning.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I was stripped of all my amateur accomplishments due to being a professional the first day I laced my boots, brother.

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? I’m currently a 4-stripe purple belt in BJJ.

Any belts/ ranks in striking disciplines? Trained in Taekwondo since I was 6 years old. Never graded.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to the University of West England and secured a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management

I love my family very much and I’m so proud to represent them on the world’s biggest stage. I took my dream in honor of my late father and turned it into reality. Nobody can ever take that away from me. Everything from here on out is a bonus. I love it.

A favorite quote of mine is “no one gives it to you. You have to take it”.

And I took it. Dana left the vault open for 15 minutes on August 22, 2023. And I made sure I got out of there with the money.

Born to fight, fight to kill. Ready to die but I never will.

This sport has my heart, both as a fighter and a fan.

I’ve made it to the show. Now I’ll show you who I am.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I originally moved to Wisconsin for wrestling in 2011 with my current wrestling coach Benjamin Tones. Ben was my college wrestling coach and was also coaching fighters at an MMA gym on the side. During the off-season Ben brought me into the fight gym and introduced me to the head coach Reese Shaner. Reese then taught me the fundamentals of martial arts.

What ranks and titles have you held? Three-time state place winner and I was a first-year National qualifier in college. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Khabib Nurmagomedov is my favorite fighter because of his mentality and mindset towards the sport. 

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My heroes are my mother and Jesus. 

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? To fight in the UFC means everything to me because it gives me the power to obtain positive changes within my community, and for the children at my school to see you can do anything you set your mind to. If my students physically see someone they know who came from the same background as them making big accomplishments, they will have no excuse to not do the same. 

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? The fight between me and Charles Johnson was the key fight in my career mainly because Charles has always been a dynamic fighter and he pushed me physically and mentally. I had to dig deep in order to get that win.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I attended one full year and then the wrestling program was shut down. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I was an assistant teacher. 

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? XFO Amateur champion.

What are your current ranks martial arts? Black Belt in Kickboxing and two-stripe purple belt in Jiu-Jitsu 

Favorite grappling technique: Triangle 

Favorite striking technique: Head kick or knees

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I would like to use my platform to benefit children all over the world by motivating and teaching them that with hard work and dedication you could achieve anything you want in life. 

Beyond a championship and money, what motivates you? It’s nice waking up every single day knowing I don’t need to report to a boss at a typical 9-to-5 day job. I can wake up every single day and do what I love. Just being able to enjoy life the way I want is motivation enough. 

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Outside of fighting, I’m deeply passionate about God. I don’t identify as any religion, but I try to remain close though. I’m not perfect. God assures me that I don’t need to be. I focus on personal growth, discipline, and building long-term impact. I spend a lot of time creating content, mentoring youth through my WOLF program, and speaking to young people about self control, accountability, and leadership. I enjoy breaking down fights, studying the mental side of competition, and helping others strengthen their mindset. I’m also passionate about building brands, especially in areas connected to fitness, lifestyle, and culture. Training is still a major part of my daily life, but outside the gym I value reflection, and staying grounded. I enjoy simple routines that sharpen focus and consistency rather than distractions.

What is one thing that you want UFC fans to know about you? I livestream every single day on TikTok, so if fans want to hop into my livestream and get to know me more that would be awesome. I have hundreds of people that hop in the livestream from all different avenues, a lot of them are fighters coming up in the game who would like advice on what to do and what not to do, so I share insights on fighting and just the mentality you need in life in order to be successful.

TRAINING: I trained at Duke Rufus Academy in Milwaukee, Dan Hendersons in San Diego and the UFC institute in LasVagas. Got to spar and work with Gerald Meerschaert, Belal Mohammad, CM Punk, Sam Alvey and Sean Strickland. Also got to go to the UFC institute to test and master my cardio max.

When and why did you start training for fighting? Since I was about maybe six in regard to teaching myself via martial arts movies. (Laughs) When I was 12, I was introduced to Karate and took it for a year via a free program my middle school had. That program later closed down and when I asked my parents to help fund and plug me into Karate further, they told me to focus on my studies. When I got my first job at 16/17 at McDonald’s, I decided to fund myself in Taekwondo. I never stopped training in Taekwondo. I later picked up and expanded on my MMA skills when I entered college at SUNY Morrisville and Oneonta via a sports club. After I graduated, I never stopped investing in my hobby and here I am today. #FightForYourDream

What ranks and titles have you held? Ring of Combat 185-lb Champion, black belt in BJJ under Jose Luis Castro Cadeamartori,  various medals in Taekwondo and BJJ tournaments, Black Prajied in Chute Boxe Muay Thai, Black Belt in Taekwondo, Black Sash in Kung Fu.  

Do you have any heroes?
